genres.name: Jungle
genres.description: Jungle emerged from the British rave scene in the early 1990s, combining chopped Amen-break drums at 160–180 BPM with deep reggae basslines, ragga vocal samples, and pitched sub-bass. It was the direct precursor to drum and bass and one of the UK's most significant dance-music inventions.
genres.summary: UK genre fusing fast chopped breakbeats with reggae sub-bass and ragga vocals, born from the early-1990s rave scene…

genres.name: Drum and Bass
genres.description: Drum and bass grew from jungle in mid-1990s Britain, refining breakbeat tempos around 170 BPM with deeper sub-bass, sophisticated sampling, and sub-genres from liquid to neurofunk. Goldie, LTJ Bukem, and labels like Moving Shadow and Metalheadz defined its first decade.
genres.summary: Fast-tempo UK electronic genre built on frenetic breakbeats and deep sub-bass, evolved from jungle in the mid-1990s…

genres.name: UK Garage
genres.description: UK Garage emerged in mid-1990s London from US house and New Jersey garage styles, characterised by shuffled 4/4 rhythms, pitch-shifted vocal chops, and heavy sub-bass. It was the parent genre of two-step, grime, bassline, and dubstep.
genres.summary: London dance genre evolved from US garage house, featuring shuffled rhythms and pitch-shifted vocals — parent of grime, two-step, and dubstep…

genres.name: Two-Step Garage
genres.description: Two-step is the pop-crossover arm of UK garage, defined by a syncopated kick pattern, pitched-up diva vocals, and romantic themes. Craig David, Artful Dodger, and Oxide & Neutrino gave it mainstream chart success around 1999–2001.
genres.summary: Polished pop subgenre of UK garage with syncopated kicks and pitched vocals, reaching UK mainstream charts around 2000…

genres.name: Grime
genres.description: Grime emerged in early-2000s East London, blending UK garage's rhythmic template with rapid-fire MC vocals over angular, minimalist 140-BPM beats. Dizzee Rascal, Wiley, Skepta, and Stormzy carried it from pirate radio to global recognition and Mercury Prize wins.
genres.summary: East London genre combining MC-driven rapid lyrics with angular 140-BPM beats, from pirate radio origins to global acclaim…

genres.name: UK Drill
genres.description: UK Drill began in South London around 2012, adapting Chicago drill's heavy 808 bass and dark minor-key melodies to British street experience, with sliding trap hi-hats and heavily auto-tuned vocals. Headie One, Digga D, and 67 brought it to the UK top ten by the late 2010s.
genres.summary: South London genre adapting Chicago drill's dark 808 production to British street realities, dominant in UK charts from around 2018…

genres.name: Dubstep
genres.description: Dubstep emerged from South London's underground around 2001, fusing UK garage's rhythmic template with dub's cavernous sub-bass in half-time beats at 140 BPM. Skream, Benga, and Digital Mystikz defined the original dark, minimal sound before international commercial offshoots took hold.
genres.summary: South London electronic genre fusing UK garage rhythms with dub sub-bass and half-time beats — the dark original sound before global commercial mutation…

genres.name: Breakbeat Hardcore
genres.description: Breakbeat hardcore dominated UK raves in 1990–1992, combining sped-up sampled breakbeats with hooky piano riffs, pitched-up vocal samples, and heavyweight bass drops. It spawned jungle, drum and bass, and happy hardcore, making it arguably the most generative UK dance genre ever.
genres.summary: UK rave music of 1990–1992 built on fast breakbeats, piano stabs, and pitched vocals — direct parent of jungle and drum and bass…

genres.name: Happy Hardcore
genres.description: Happy hardcore branched from breakbeat hardcore in the early 1990s, pushing tempos to 160–180 BPM with euphoric major-key melodies and chipmunk-pitched vocals. It thrived in UK warehouse raves and later in Australia, producing dedicated club nights and independent labels still active today.
genres.summary: UK rave subgenre with fast tempos, euphoric melodies, and pitched-up vocals, a fixture of warehouse parties and still active in underground clubs…

genres.name: Rave
genres.description: UK rave culture and its acid-house, techno, and breakbeat soundtrack exploded in 1988–1992 across illegal warehouse parties, seeding almost every subsequent UK dance genre. The second summer of love made rave a mass phenomenon that transformed British youth culture.
genres.summary: UK late-1980s mass movement of illegal warehouse parties playing acid house and breakbeat, seeding jungle, drum and bass, and the modern club scene…

genres.name: Big Beat
genres.description: Big beat blended breakbeats and hip-hop samples with distorted guitars and rock energy, peaking in the UK in the late 1990s via Chemical Brothers, Fatboy Slim, Prodigy, and the Wall of Sound label. Its crossover appeal made it one of the decade's best-selling dance styles.
genres.summary: Mid-1990s UK genre combining loud breakbeats, hip-hop samples, and rock guitars — the Chemical Brothers and Fatboy Slim sound of stadium dance…

genres.name: Intelligent Dance Music
genres.description: IDM emerged from UK and US electronica in the early 1990s, prioritising complex rhythmic structures, unusual timbres, and emotional depth over dancefloor function. Warp Records — home to Aphex Twin, Autechre, and Boards of Canada — became its central institution.
genres.summary: Cerebral electronic music emphasising rhythmic complexity and texture, centred on Warp Records and figures like Aphex Twin since the early 1990s…

genres.name: Bleep Techno
genres.description: Bleep techno originated in Sheffield and Leeds around 1989, featuring stark synthesised basslines, sparse percussion, and ascending high-pitched synth tones. Warp Records' early releases by LFO and Forgemasters defined this distinctly northern English take on electronic dance music.
genres.summary: Yorkshire-born electronic music defined by deep bass drops and piercing synth bleeps, an early Warp Records sound from 1989…

genres.name: Progressive House
genres.description: Progressive house developed from house music in early-1990s UK, defined by long evolving structures, gradual filter sweeps, and atmospheric synthesiser layers. Sasha, John Digweed, and labels like Guerrilla and Platipus built its reputation as a sophisticated alternative to mainstream rave.
genres.summary: Long-form, melodically evolving UK house from the early 1990s — Sasha and John Digweed's genre, influential on the global trance scene…

genres.name: Trip Hop
genres.description: Trip hop emerged from Bristol in the early 1990s, fusing hip-hop's slow dusty beats with atmospheric samples, jazz textures, and melancholic vocals. Massive Attack, Portishead, and Tricky defined its introspective, cinematic character and enduring critical prestige.
genres.summary: Bristol-born genre fusing slow hip-hop beats, jazz samples, and melancholic vocals — Massive Attack, Portishead, and Tricky are its defining acts…

genres.name: Afroswing
genres.description: Afroswing emerged in the UK mid-2010s, blending Afrobeats' Nigerian-influenced melodies with grime and R&B production. J Hus, Kojo Funds, and Afro B gave it a distinct presence on UK charts, while MoStack and Hardy Caprio broadened its mainstream reach.
genres.summary: UK fusion of Afrobeats melody with grime and R&B production, emerging around 2016 through J Hus and reaching the mainstream by 2018…

genres.name: UK Hip-Hop
genres.description: UK hip-hop evolved from American imports in the early 1980s into a distinct British identity through the 1990s–2000s underground, with Roots Manuva, Taskforce, and Skinnyman bringing regional voices and class politics. It is the cultural root of grime, UK drill, and the modern British rap mainstream.
genres.summary: British hip-hop with distinct regional voices, evolving from 1980s imports through a 1990s–2000s underground to its role as parent of grime and UK drill…

genres.name: UK R&B
genres.description: UK R&B developed a distinct British character from American R&B and UK garage in the late 1990s through Craig David and Ms Dynamite, later fusing with grime, Afroswing, and contemporary production in the 2010s via Ella Mai, Mahalia, and Jorja Smith.
genres.summary: British R&B blending American soul influences with UK urban production styles from Craig David and Ms Dynamite to Jorja Smith and Mahalia…

genres.name: Bassline
genres.description: Bassline (niche or 4×4) developed in Sheffield, Leeds, and Nottingham from UK garage, distinguished by a four-to-the-floor kick, heavy rolling bass riffs, and vocal samples. It dominated northern English club scenes in the mid-2000s before spreading nationally.
genres.summary: Northern English dance genre evolved from UK garage with pounding 4/4 kicks and heavy bass riffs, the sound of northern clubs in the mid-2000s…

genres.name: Future Garage
genres.description: Future garage revived UK garage's shuffled rhythms around 2008 with spacious, atmospheric production, pitched vocal chops, and deep sub-bass. Burial's influence — particularly Untrue — defined the genre's melancholic, introspective character.
genres.summary: UK electronic genre reviving garage rhythms with atmospheric depth and melancholic pitched vocals, Burial's Untrue as its touchstone…

genres.name: UK Funky
genres.description: UK Funky emerged in London around 2007–2009, fusing UK garage's shuffled rhythms with Afrobeats, soca, and Nigerian percussion. Centred on East London pirate radio, it produced a short but influential wave of energetic dancefloor music led by producers like Roska and Cooly G.
genres.summary: London dancefloor genre blending UK garage rhythms with Afrobeats and Caribbean percussion, thriving on East London pirate radio around 2008…

genres.name: Broken Beat
genres.description: Broken beat developed in London at the turn of the millennium, combining jazz harmony and soul sensibility with complex polyrhythmic breakbeats and synthesiser bass. Labels like Atone and artists such as 4hero, Kaidi Tatham, and IG Culture formed a small but influential scene.
genres.summary: London jazz-electronic hybrid with polyrhythmic breakbeats and sophisticated harmony, a small but influential movement from the late 1990s…

genres.name: Post-Dubstep
genres.description: Post-dubstep describes artists who absorbed dubstep's sparse rhythms and heavy sub-bass into more song-focused contexts, incorporating R&B and soul. James Blake, Jamie Woon, and Mount Kimbie were its defining voices, and it was one of the most critically acclaimed UK sounds of the early 2010s.
genres.summary: Early-2010s UK movement absorbing dubstep's production techniques into intimate, soul-influenced song forms — James Blake and Mount Kimbie as key figures…

genres.name: UK Bass
genres.description: UK bass is an umbrella for bass-heavy UK electronic music from the 2010s that defies sub-genre classification — blending footwork, grime instrumentals, and experimental club tracks. Labels such as Hyperdub, Hessle Audio, and Night Slugs were its institutional centres.
genres.summary: Umbrella term for experimentally inclined bass-heavy UK electronic music from Hyperdub and Night Slugs in the early 2010s…

genres.name: UK Hardcore
genres.description: UK hardcore settled into a distinct style by 1993–1994 with 4/4 kicks, euphoric synthesiser leads, and layered breakbeats at 150–180 BPM. It remained active in the UK underground through dedicated labels like Evolution Records and massive club events like Slammin' Vinyl.
genres.summary: UK dance genre combining hard 4/4 kicks with euphoric synth leads and fast breakbeats, active from the mid-1990s rave era through to today…

genres.name: Post-Punk
genres.description: Post-punk extended punk's energy into experimental territory, incorporating art rock, funk, dub, and electronics while keeping DIY independence. Gang of Four, Wire, Joy Division, PiL, and Talking Heads redefined the limits of guitar-based music and seeded indie rock, gothic rock, and new wave.
genres.summary: Late-1970s genre pushing punk into experimental art-rock, funk, and dub, with Gang of Four, Joy Division, and Wire as its defining acts…

genres.name: New Wave
genres.description: New wave grew from punk into a danceable, keyboard-driven pop form in the late 1970s and early 1980s, dominating British and American charts with acts like Talking Heads, Blondie, Duran Duran, and The Police. Its embrace of synthesisers and slick production distinguished it from raw punk.
genres.summary: Pop-driven offshoot of punk combining electronic keyboards with catchy hooks — Talking Heads, Blondie, and Duran Duran's genre…

genres.name: Britpop
genres.description: Britpop was a mid-1990s UK guitar-pop movement reasserting British musical identity against American grunge, drawing on Mod and Kinks influences. The Blur–Oasis chart battle of 1995 was a national event, and Pulp, Elastica, and Supergrass were among its principal voices.
genres.summary: Mid-1990s UK guitar-pop movement asserting British identity through Mod and 1960s influences — the Blur vs. Oasis era…

genres.name: Shoegaze
genres.description: Shoegaze emerged from UK alternative rock in the late 1980s, defined by densely layered guitars with heavy tremolo, walls of distortion, and often buried vocals. My Bloody Valentine's Loveless (1991) is its benchmark, while Ride, Slowdive, and Lush defined the surrounding scene.
genres.summary: UK indie genre built on layered tremolo guitars and hazy vocals, with My Bloody Valentine's Loveless as the definitive statement…

genres.name: Madchester
genres.description: Madchester was a late-1980s Manchester scene fusing indie guitars with the energy of acid house, producing a euphoric, baggy groove. The Hacienda club was its crucible; the Happy Mondays, Stone Roses, and 808 State were its principal acts.
genres.summary: Late-1980s Manchester scene merging indie guitars with acid house energy — the Stone Roses, Happy Mondays, and the Hacienda club…

genres.name: Indie Rock
genres.description: Indie rock emerged from post-punk as guitar music released on independent labels, evolving from a distribution category to a stylistic one. It spans jangly college rock (REM, The Smiths) to lo-fi noise (Pavement, Guided by Voices) to polished indie anthems (Arcade Fire, Arctic Monkeys).
genres.summary: Guitar-led rock originating on independent labels in the 1980s, encompassing decades of alternative styles from The Smiths to Arctic Monkeys…

genres.name: Indie Pop
genres.description: Indie pop distils indie rock's independent ethos into a melodically brighter, more hook-driven form rooted in 1960s pop, jangly guitar, and C86 aesthetics. Belle and Sebastian, The Pastels, Camera Obscura, and later Alvvays carry the lineage.
genres.summary: Melodically bright, jangly pop subgenre of indie rooted in the 1980s C86 cassette scene and 1960s pop influences…

genres.name: Gothic Rock
genres.description: Gothic rock grew from post-punk in the late 1970s UK, adopting darker aesthetics — minor-key basslines, atmospheric guitar, operatic vocals, and morbid themes. Bauhaus, Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Sisters of Mercy created the foundation of goth subculture.
genres.summary: Dark UK post-punk offshoot defined by minor-key atmospherics and theatrical vocals — the musical foundation of goth subculture…

genres.name: Darkwave
genres.description: Darkwave fused gothic rock's dark atmospherics with synthesiser textures and minimal electronic production, creating brooding, melancholic music. Clan of Xymox, Dead Can Dance, and This Mortal Coil were its key acts across UK and European scenes.
genres.summary: Dark electronic-rock genre blending goth aesthetics with synthesisers, spanning UK and European underground scenes from the early 1980s…

genres.name: Northern Soul
genres.description: Northern soul was a UK working-class dance movement from the late 1960s centred on rare American soul 45s that the mainstream market had overlooked. The Wigan Casino and Twisted Wheel in Manchester were its temples, and its athletic dance style became a defining subcultural marker.
genres.summary: Northern English dance movement of the late 1960s built around rare American soul singles, with the Wigan Casino as its spiritual home…

genres.name: UK Soul
genres.description: UK soul describes British artists recording soul, R&B, and jazz-influenced pop from the mid-1980s onwards — from Sade and Soul II Soul's international breakthrough to Amy Winehouse and Adele. It blends American soul traditions with understated British sensibility.
genres.summary: British soul tradition from Sade and Soul II Soul in the 1980s to Amy Winehouse and Adele, blending American influences with British refinement…

genres.name: 2 Tone
genres.description: 2 Tone was a late-1970s UK movement centred on The Specials' Coventry label, fusing ska and rocksteady with punk energy. The Specials, Madness, and Selecter paired anti-racist messaging with irresistibly danceable music, and the movement remains one of Britain's most politically significant pop moments.
genres.summary: Late-1970s UK ska-punk fusion from The Specials' Coventry label, combining anti-racist politics with infectious danceable energy…

genres.name: Dream Pop
genres.description: Dream pop evolved from post-punk and new wave in the mid-1980s UK, prioritising lush reverb-soaked guitars, introspective vocals, and atmospheric layering. Cocteau Twins and This Mortal Coil were its founding figures; Beach House and Mazzy Star carried the aesthetic into the 21st century.
genres.summary: Atmospheric pop built on reverb-saturated guitars and ethereal vocals, rooted in 1980s UK indie with Cocteau Twins as its archetype…

genres.name: Post-Rock
genres.description: Post-rock uses rock instruments — guitars, bass, drums — to create largely instrumental music organised around texture, dynamics, and slow-build crescendos rather than songs and solos. Bark Psychosis, Slint, Mogwai, and Godspeed You! Black Emperor are its canonical acts.
genres.summary: Instrumental genre using rock instruments to explore gradual dynamics and texture rather than traditional songs — Mogwai and Godspeed You! Black Emperor as touchstones…

genres.name: Britcore
genres.description: Britcore was a UK hip-hop movement of the late 1980s and early 1990s combining American hip-hop production with aggressive British lyricism, often politically engaged. Silver Bullet, Ruthless Rap Assassins, and Gunshot were key figures in this short-lived but influential underground.
genres.summary: Aggressive, politically conscious UK hip-hop from the late 1980s blending American production with confrontational British MC culture…

genres.name: Techno
genres.description: Techno originated in Detroit in the mid-1980s through Juan Atkins, Derrick May, and Kevin Saunderson, synthesising European electronic music, Chicago house, and Afrofuturist ideology into repetitive, machine-driven dance music. It arrived in Berlin after reunification and became the heartbeat of global club culture.
genres.summary: Detroit-born electronic dance music built on repetitive 4/4 beats and synthesisers — became the defining sound of Berlin's post-Wall club culture…

genres.name: Berlin Techno
genres.description: Berlin techno developed after German reunification in 1989, when derelict East Berlin buildings became venues for all-night parties. Artists like Hardfloor and Tanith, later Berghain residents, built a harder, darker, more industrial sound than Detroit's original, and Berlin became the world capital of club culture.
genres.summary: Dark, industrial techno style born in post-reunification East Berlin warehouses — Berghain is its temple and the global benchmark for club culture…

genres.name: Minimal Techno
genres.description: Minimal techno stripped the genre to its bare elements — subtle rhythmic variations, sparse textures, and long hypnotic structures. Richie Hawtin (Plastikman), Basic Channel, and Robert Hood defined its aesthetic in the mid-1990s, and it influenced the microhouse and tech-house movements that followed.
genres.summary: Stripped-down techno emphasising subtle rhythmic variation and hypnotic repetition, pioneered by Richie Hawtin and Basic Channel in the mid-1990s…

genres.name: Eurodance
genres.description: Eurodance dominated European pop charts in the early 1990s with hooky synthesiser riffs, female sung choruses, male rap verses, and hard-hitting beats at 130–160 BPM. Acts like Ace of Base, 2 Unlimited, Snap!, and Haddaway sold tens of millions of records globally.
genres.summary: European pop-dance genre with sing-along synth hooks and rap verses, dominating charts across Europe and worldwide in the early 1990s…

genres.name: Electronic Body Music
genres.description: EBM emerged from Belgium and Germany in the early 1980s, combining industrial electronic textures with hard metronomic beats and aggressive vocalisations to produce a physically demanding dancefloor sound. Front 242, Nitzer Ebb, and D.A.F. defined its aesthetic.
genres.summary: Belgian-German dance genre fusing industrial electronics with hard beats — Front 242 and Nitzer Ebb's body-centred club music from the 1980s…

genres.name: Gabber
genres.description: Gabber emerged in Rotterdam in the early 1990s as an extreme, high-tempo hardcore techno subgenre, with distorted bass drum kicks at 160–220 BPM and heavy synthesiser stabs. Rotterdam clubs and labels like Rotterdam Records created a distinct working-class rave culture.
genres.summary: Rotterdam's extreme hardcore techno with distorted kicks at 160+ BPM and aggressive aesthetics, born in early-1990s Netherlands…

genres.name: Hardcore Techno
genres.description: Hardcore techno pushed dance music tempos and intensity to extremes in the early 1990s, encompassing Rotterdam gabber, Belgian new beat mutations, and related high-BPM styles. It spawned hardstyle, industrial hardcore, and speedcore, with a dedicated global following.
genres.summary: Umbrella term for extreme-tempo, aggressive electronic dance music that spawned gabber, hardstyle, and industrial hardcore in the early 1990s…

genres.name: Hardstyle
genres.description: Hardstyle emerged from the Netherlands in the early 2000s, combining hard kick drums with melodic synthesiser leads at 140–160 BPM. It developed its own massive festival circuit — Qlimax, Defqon.1 — and a dedicated global fanbase, making it the most commercially successful offshoot of hardcore techno.
genres.summary: Dutch hard-electronic genre with melodic synth leads and powerful kicks, with its own festival circuit and global following since the early 2000s…

genres.name: Progressive Trance
genres.description: Progressive trance developed in the mid-1990s from progressive house and European trance, defined by long gradual builds, layered synthesiser arpeggios, and euphoric releases. BT, Sasha, and labels like Platipus and Hooj Choons shaped its evolution, and it became one of the biggest festival sounds of the late 1990s.
genres.summary: Long-form trance subgenre built on gradual synth-arpeggio builds and euphoric climaxes, one of the biggest festival sounds of the late 1990s…

genres.name: Psytrance
genres.description: Psytrance grew from the Goa trance scene of the early 1990s, combining fast tempos (140–150 BPM) with layered synthesiser sequences and mind-altering sonic textures aimed at trance-inducing dancefloor experiences. Israel's outdoor festival culture became its global home.
genres.summary: Fast, hypnotic trance rooted in Goa beach parties and Israeli festival culture, built on layered synth sequences at 140–150 BPM…

genres.name: Krautrock
genres.description: Krautrock was a West German experimental rock movement rejecting Anglo-American conventions in favour of motorik rhythms, long improvised passages, and electronic textures. Can, Kraftwerk, Neu!, Faust, and Tangerine Dream were its central acts, and its influence on post-punk, electronic music, and ambient was enormous.
genres.summary: West German experimental rock movement of 1968–1978 blending motorik rhythms, improvisation, and electronics — foundational to post-punk and electronic music…

genres.name: Neue Deutsche Welle
genres.description: Neue Deutsche Welle (NDW) was Germany's new wave movement from the late 1970s to the mid-1980s, producing German-language punk and synth-pop with humour and absurdist lyrics. Nena, Trio, and Falco crossed over to international charts.
genres.summary: German-language new wave of 1979–1984, producing quirky synth-pop and punk hits — Nena's '99 Luftballons' and Trio's 'Da Da Da'…

genres.name: Deutschrap
genres.description: Deutschrap (German rap) emerged with German-language hip-hop in the early 1990s through Advanced Chemistry and Die Fantastischen Vier, evolving into Germany's dominant pop genre by the 2010s through Capital Bra, Shindy, and Sido.
genres.summary: German-language hip-hop from 1990s underground origins to 2010s mainstream dominance, the biggest-selling popular music genre in modern Germany…

genres.name: Industrial
genres.description: Industrial music emerged from conceptual art and electronic experimentation in the mid-1970s, pioneered by Throbbing Gristle and later Einstürzende Neubauten, using noise, tape manipulation, and confrontational imagery to interrogate society. It seeded EBM, power electronics, noise, and metal crossovers.
genres.summary: Experimental genre rooted in noise, tape manipulation, and provocative art — Throbbing Gristle and Einstürzende Neubauten's confrontational sound from the mid-1970s…

genres.name: Dutch House
genres.description: Dutch house emerged around 2008 as a percussive, melodically catchy variant of electro house and progressive house, driven by Tiësto, Afrojack, Nicky Romero, and Martin Garrix. It became a dominant strand of mainstream EDM worldwide in the 2010s.
genres.summary: Energetic Dutch electro-house style dominant in mainstream EDM in the 2010s, exemplified by Tiësto, Afrojack, and Martin Garrix…

genres.name: Blues
genres.description: Blues is an African-American genre from the Deep South rooted in spirituals, work songs, and field hollers, crystallised in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Its twelve-bar form, blue notes, and emotional guitar and vocal expression became the foundation of rock, jazz, soul, and virtually all Western popular music.
genres.summary: African-American genre from the Deep South built on twelve-bar forms and blue notes — the root of rock, jazz, soul, and all modern Western popular music…

genres.name: Jazz
genres.description: Jazz emerged in New Orleans around the turn of the 20th century from African-American blues, ragtime, gospel, and European harmonics. Its emphasis on improvisation, swing feel, and collective interplay made it one of the most intellectually rich and globally influential music forms of the century, spawning bebop, fusion, free jazz, and dozens of regional variants.
genres.summary: African-American genre born in New Orleans from blues and ragtime — defined by improvisation and swing, one of the 20th century's most globally influential forms…

genres.name: Country
genres.description: Country music developed in rural America and Appalachia in the 1920s from folk ballads, old-time string bands, blues, and gospel. From Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family through Hank Williams and Johnny Cash to Taylor Swift, it remains one of America's most commercially dominant genres.
genres.summary: American genre from Appalachian folk and blues, spanning Jimmie Rodgers and Hank Williams to modern billion-stream country pop…

genres.name: Folk
genres.description: Folk music encompasses the traditional acoustic musical traditions of communities, transmitted orally across generations. The US folk revival of the 1950s–60s — Pete Seeger, Woody Guthrie, Bob Dylan — turned it into a vehicle for social protest; the UK tradition runs from Cecil Sharp through Fairport Convention to contemporary folk-rock.
genres.summary: Acoustic communal music transmitted through generations — the 1950s–60s American folk revival turned it into a vehicle for social change through Dylan and Guthrie…

genres.name: Rock and Roll
genres.description: Rock and roll emerged from African-American blues, gospel, and country in the early 1950s. Chuck Berry, Little Richard, and Elvis Presley fused boogie-woogie and R&B into an electrifying form that became the most transformative youth music movement of the 20th century and the foundation of virtually all subsequent Western popular music.
genres.summary: American genre fusing blues, gospel, and country in the early 1950s — Chuck Berry, Little Richard, and Elvis Presley's revolution that changed popular music forever…

genres.name: Psychedelic Rock
genres.description: Psychedelic rock emerged mid-1960s in the US and UK, using studio manipulation, distorted guitars, and extended structures to evoke altered states. Jimi Hendrix, Jefferson Airplane, Pink Floyd, and The Beatles' late work defined its many variants, seeding progressive rock, heavy metal, and alternative music.
genres.summary: Mid-1960s rock using studio experimentation and distorted guitars to evoke altered states — foundational to progressive rock, heavy metal, and alternative music…

genres.name: Punk Rock
genres.description: Punk rock emerged in New York and London in the mid-1970s as a raw, aggressive rejection of progressive and classic rock excess. The Ramones, Sex Pistols, and The Clash established short fast songs, distorted guitars, and DIY ethos that spawned post-punk, hardcore, and alternative rock.
genres.summary: Mid-1970s genre defined by short fast songs, distorted guitars, and radical DIY ethos — the Ramones, Sex Pistols, and Clash launched a decades-long counterculture…

genres.name: Heavy Metal
genres.description: Heavy metal evolved from hard rock and blues-rock in the late 1960s, pioneered by Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin, and Deep Purple with loud, distorted guitars, powerful drumming, and amplified bass. Its many subgenres — glam, thrash, death, black, doom — have given it a durable global following across five decades.
genres.summary: Hard-rock offshoot of the late 1960s defined by loud distorted guitars and power — Black Sabbath and Led Zeppelin's genre, with subgenres spanning every continent…

genres.name: Grunge
genres.description: Grunge emerged from Seattle in the late 1980s, fusing heavy metal distortion with punk anger and indie rock sensibility. Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, and Alice in Chains made it the defining rock sound of the early 1990s before its rapid commercial co-option.
genres.summary: Seattle alternative rock fusing metal and punk into raw, emotionally direct music — Nirvana and Pearl Jam made it the dominant rock sound of the early 1990s…

genres.name: Alternative Rock
genres.description: Alternative rock is a broad category for guitar-led rock outside the mainstream from the late 1970s onwards, originally a chart designation that became associated with college radio, independent labels, and a DIY ethic. It went mainstream in the early 1990s with Nirvana, Radiohead, and R.E.M.
genres.summary: Broad category of guitar rock outside the mainstream, from post-punk college radio to 1990s Nirvana and Radiohead, rooted in independent-label culture…

genres.name: Emo
genres.description: Emo (emotional hardcore) evolved from Washington DC's hardcore punk scene in the mid-1980s, emphasising confessional, emotionally intense lyrics. It moved from underground (Sunny Day Real Estate, Jawbreaker) to 2000s pop-punk mainstream via My Chemical Romance and Fall Out Boy.
genres.summary: Genre rooted in confessional lyrics and post-hardcore energy, from DC underground origins to global 2000s pop-punk mainstream…

genres.name: Pop Punk
genres.description: Pop punk fuses punk rock's guitar energy with melodic hooks, pioneered by Green Day and The Offspring in the early 1990s and dominant in the 2000s mainstream through Blink-182, Sum 41, and Paramore.
genres.summary: Melodic punk-rock hybrid dominant in 1990s–2000s rock mainstream through Green Day and Blink-182…

genres.name: R&B
genres.description: Rhythm and blues emerged in 1940s African-American communities as a commercialisation of jazz, blues, and gospel for dance. Its evolution through soul, funk, new jack swing, and contemporary production made it one of the most continuously dominant forces in American popular music.
genres.summary: African-American genre synthesising jazz, blues, and gospel into danceable popular forms, evolving through eight decades to remain at the heart of popular music…

genres.name: Gospel
genres.description: Gospel music is African-American Christian music rooted in church traditions, drawing on blues, spirituals, and hymns. Thomas A. Dorsey codified gospel as a genre in the 1920s, and it has been the emotional and musical bedrock of soul, R&B, and rock and roll.
genres.summary: African-American Christian music tradition blending spirituals, blues, and choir performance — the foundational bedrock of soul, R&B, and rock and roll…

genres.name: Americana
genres.description: Americana is a contemporary US roots genre drawing on country, folk, blues, and rock traditions with a focus on songwriting and authenticity. Wilco, Ryan Adams, and the Americana Music Association formalised it in the late 1990s as a distinct alternative to mainstream country.
genres.summary: Contemporary US roots genre blending country, folk, and blues with a songwriter-centred ethos, formalised as a category in the late 1990s…

genres.name: Neo Soul
genres.description: Neo soul emerged in the mid-1990s US as a revival of classic soul's artistry — warm analogue textures, complex harmony, and emotionally rich vocals — combined with hip-hop and funk production. D'Angelo, Erykah Badu, Maxwell, and Lauryn Hill defined its aesthetic and earned it critical acclaim.
genres.summary: Mid-1990s US movement reviving classic soul's emotional depth with hip-hop and funk production — D'Angelo, Erykah Badu, and Lauryn Hill as its defining voices…

genres.name: Lo-Fi Hip-Hop
genres.description: Lo-fi hip-hop draws on boom bap and jazz rap traditions but prioritises warm dusty production — vinyl crackle, muffled drums, and jazzy samples — over dancefloor energy. It became a ubiquitous streaming phenomenon in the 2010s through YouTube live-radio channels and playlist culture.
genres.summary: Relaxed, sample-based hip-hop combining jazz harmonies with vintage tape aesthetics — a dominant streaming phenomenon of the 2010s through YouTube 'study music' channels…

genres.name: Blues Rock
genres.description: Blues rock fused American blues guitar forms with rock instrumentation and energy, pioneered in the UK by the Rolling Stones and Yardbirds and in the US by Jimi Hendrix and ZZ Top. It bridged traditional blues and hard rock and gave rise to heavy metal.
genres.summary: Genre fusing American blues guitar with rock instrumentation and energy — the Rolling Stones and Yardbirds' meeting point between blues and hard rock…

genres.name: Rockabilly
genres.description: Rockabilly was one of the earliest rock and roll styles, fusing country, blues, and boogie-woogie with slap bass and echo-heavy guitar, pioneered at Sun Records by Elvis Presley, Carl Perkins, and Jerry Lee Lewis. It remains the sonic template for countless revival acts.
genres.summary: Early rock and roll fusion of country, blues, and boogie-woogie born at Sun Records — Elvis Presley, Carl Perkins, and Jerry Lee Lewis in the mid-1950s…

genres.name: Synth-Pop
genres.description: Synth-pop emerged from British post-punk and new wave in the late 1970s, replacing rock instruments with synthesisers and drum machines to create a cool, futuristic pop. Kraftwerk's electronic aesthetic, channelled through Human League, Depeche Mode, and Erasure, defined the form.
genres.summary: UK-pioneered pop genre replacing guitars with synthesisers and drum machines — the Human League, Depeche Mode, and Pet Shop Boys' world…

genres.name: Post-Hardcore
genres.description: Post-hardcore evolved from US hardcore punk in the mid-1980s, maintaining intense energy while exploring more complex song structures, emotional depth, and unconventional sounds. Fugazi, At the Drive-In, Refused, and Hum are key acts; it seeded emo, screamo, and math rock.
genres.summary: US genre extending hardcore punk's intensity into complex, emotionally expansive song forms — Fugazi and At the Drive-In as its canonical acts…

genres.name: Hardcore Punk
genres.description: Hardcore punk emerged in the late 1970s US and UK as a faster, more aggressive evolution of punk rock, with Black Flag, Dead Kennedys, and Minor Threat as defining acts. Its DIY ethics produced a global network of independent labels, zines, and all-ages venues that continues to this day.
genres.summary: Faster, more aggressive punk variant from the late 1970s US — Black Flag, Dead Kennedys, and Minor Threat's DIY underground network…

genres.name: Bebop
genres.description: Bebop emerged in early-1940s New York as a radical reimagining of jazz, emphasising virtuosity, complex harmonic progressions, and fast tempos as a vehicle for improvisation rather than dance. Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie, Thelonious Monk, and Miles Davis defined its vocabulary.
genres.summary: Early-1940s New York jazz revolution emphasising virtuosic improvisation and complex harmony — Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie's genre…

genres.name: Swing
genres.description: Swing was the dominant popular music of the USA in the 1930s and early 1940s, played by large orchestras and featuring syncopated rhythms, arranged horn sections, and a driving groove that became a national dance craze. Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, and Glenn Miller led the swing era.
genres.summary: American popular music of the 1930s–40s played by big bands — Benny Goodman, Duke Ellington, and Glenn Miller's era of mass dance music…

genres.name: Delta Blues
genres.description: Delta blues is the foundational blues style from the Mississippi Delta region, characterised by raw vocals, slide guitar, and call-and-response forms. Robert Johnson, Charley Patton, and Son House are its iconic figures, and their recordings — many made in the 1930s — remain among the most influential in American music.
genres.summary: Raw, slide-guitar-driven blues from the Mississippi Delta — Robert Johnson and Son House's foundational recordings from the 1920s–30s…

genres.name: Chicago Blues
genres.description: Chicago blues developed from the Delta blues brought north by the Great Migration, adding electric guitar, amplification, harmonica, and a rhythm section. Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, Little Walter, and Chess Records created a louder, urban sound that directly inspired British rock and roll.
genres.summary: Electric, amplified blues developed in Chicago by Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf — the direct inspiration for the British rock and roll explosion…

genres.name: Jazz Fusion
genres.description: Jazz fusion emerged in the late 1960s as jazz musicians incorporated rock's electric instruments, amplification, and groove into jazz improvisation. Miles Davis' Bitches Brew (1970), Weather Report, and Mahavishnu Orchestra were its defining forces, creating music of extraordinary rhythmic complexity.
genres.summary: Late-1960s hybrid fusing jazz improvisation with rock's electric instruments and groove — Miles Davis' Bitches Brew and Weather Report as touchstones…

genres.name: Smooth Jazz
genres.description: Smooth jazz emerged from jazz fusion's more accessible, radio-friendly tendencies, combining jazz harmonics and improvisation with R&B and pop grooves. Kenny G, Grover Washington Jr., Dave Koz, and Bob James brought it to mass commercial success in the 1980s and 1990s.
genres.summary: Commercially accessible jazz variant blending improvisation with R&B and pop grooves — Kenny G and Grover Washington Jr.'s radio-friendly sound…

genres.name: Acid Jazz
genres.description: Acid jazz emerged in late-1980s London clubs, fusing jazz harmony and instrumentation with funk grooves, hip-hop sampling, and club culture. The Acid Jazz Records label, Jamiroquai, Brand New Heavies, and Incognito were its commercial face.
genres.summary: Late-1980s London genre fusing jazz harmonics with funk grooves and hip-hop sampling — Jamiroquai and Brand New Heavies' club-ready jazz revival…

genres.name: Thrash Metal
genres.description: Thrash metal emerged in the early 1980s US, combining heavy metal's guitar riffing with hardcore punk's speed and aggression. Metallica, Slayer, Megadeth, and Anthrax — the 'Big Four' — defined it, and it influenced every subsequent extreme metal style.
genres.summary: Early-1980s US genre combining metal riffs with hardcore speed — Metallica, Slayer, and the Big Four's blueprint for extreme metal…

genres.name: Death Metal
genres.description: Death metal emerged from thrash in the early 1980s with heavily distorted down-tuned guitars, blast-beat drumming, and growled or guttural vocals. Death, Morbid Angel, and Obituary in Florida, and later Scandinavian acts, developed it into a globally active extreme metal genre.
genres.summary: Extreme metal genre from early-1980s Florida featuring down-tuned guitars, blast beats, and growled vocals — Death and Morbid Angel's founding sound…

genres.name: Black Metal
genres.description: Black metal emerged in the early 1980s with Venom and Bathory, crystallising in 1990s Norway into a deliberately primitive, atmospheric style with tremolo-picked guitars, blast beats, shrieked vocals, and lo-fi production. Mayhem, Burzum, Darkthrone, and Emperor are its canonical acts.
genres.summary: Extreme metal genre crystallised in 1990s Norway featuring tremolo guitars, blast beats, and shrieked vocals — Mayhem and Burzum's lo-fi darkness…

genres.name: Doom Metal
genres.description: Doom metal takes its slow tempos, heavy riffing, and atmosphere of dread from early Black Sabbath, developing into distinct sub-styles from traditional doom to funeral doom. Candlemass, Cathedral, My Dying Bride, and Electric Wizard are key acts.
genres.summary: Slow, heavy metal subgenre rooted in early Black Sabbath, emphasising atmosphere and dread over speed — Candlemass, My Dying Bride, and Electric Wizard…

genres.name: Power Metal
genres.description: Power metal developed in the mid-1980s in Europe, combining heavy metal's guitar work with melodic, soaring vocal lines, fast tempos, and epic fantasy themes. Helloween, Blind Guardian, DragonForce, and Rhapsody defined a cheerful, bombastic alternative to extreme metal.
genres.summary: Melodic, fast, and epic heavy metal subgenre from mid-1980s Europe — Helloween and Blind Guardian's soaring vocals and fantasy themes…

genres.name: Ambient
genres.description: Ambient music prioritises atmosphere and texture over melody and rhythm, designed to be as ignorable as it is listenable. Brian Eno coined the term with Ambient 1: Music for Airports (1978), and the genre expanded through Tangerine Dream, Stars of the Lid, and thousands of electronic artists into a vast and active field.
genres.summary: Atmospheric, texture-focused electronic music coined by Brian Eno with Ambient 1 (1978) — designed to be as much environment as music…

genres.name: Vaporwave
genres.description: Vaporwave emerged as an internet-native microgenre around 2011, slowing down, pitch-shifting, and chopping smooth jazz, elevator music, and 1980s–90s commercial pop into dreamlike, ironic soundscapes. Macintosh Plus's Floral Shoppe (2011) and later James Ferraro popularised it online.
genres.summary: Internet-born microgenre of slowed, pitch-shifted 1980s–90s commercial music — Macintosh Plus's Floral Shoppe as the defining artefact…

genres.name: Hyperpop
genres.description: Hyperpop emerged from London's PC Music label and surrounding online communities, pushing pop production to extremes — heavily pitch-shifted vocals, distorted 808 beats, maximalist sound design, and internet-era aesthetics. 100 gecs, Charli XCX, and SOPHIE brought it to mainstream attention.
genres.summary: Maximalist internet pop genre from PC Music and 100 gecs pushing production to extremes with pitch-shifted vocals and distorted 808 beats…

genres.name: Synthwave
genres.description: Synthwave is a modern electronic genre drawing on the synthesiser and drum machine sounds of 1980s film scores, television, and synth-pop, evoking a nostalgic retro-futurism. Artists like Kavinsky, Perturbator, Carpenter Brut, and Gunship gained global audiences through streaming and video game soundtracks.
genres.summary: Modern electronic genre reviving 1980s synthesiser aesthetics and film-score nostalgia through Kavinsky, Perturbator, and Carpenter Brut…

genres.name: Future Bass
genres.description: Future bass emerged around 2013, combining dubstep's sub-bass influence with bright, major-key chords, chopped vocal samples, and electronic pop aesthetics. Flume, Rustie, ODESZA, and Cashmere Cat popularised it, and it became a significant streaming genre in the mid-2010s.
genres.summary: Emotionally bright electronic pop genre blending dubstep bass with chopped vocals and major-key chords — Flume and ODESZA's signature sound…

genres.name: City Pop
genres.description: City pop was a Japanese urban pop style from the late 1970s to early 1990s, characterised by polished production, sophisticated chord voicings, funk and R&B influences, and aspirational imagery of modern consumer life. Tatsuro Yamashita, Mariya Takeuchi, and Anri were its leading artists, and it experienced a major global streaming revival in the 2010s.
genres.summary: Japanese urban pop of 1977–1991 with polished production and R&B influences — Mariya Takeuchi and Tatsuro Yamashita experienced a global streaming revival in the 2010s…

genres.name: J-Rock
genres.description: J-rock (Japanese rock) encompasses the wide range of rock music produced in Japan, from the Group Sounds movement of the 1960s through 1980s–90s acts like X Japan, B'z, and BUCK-TICK, to 2000s alternative rock acts like Asian Kung-Fu Generation and ONE OK ROCK.
genres.summary: Japanese rock spanning the Group Sounds movement of the 1960s through X Japan and ONE OK ROCK, adapting Western rock traditions with Japanese aesthetics…

genres.name: Visual Kei
genres.description: Visual kei is a Japanese music movement combining theatrical performances and elaborate costumes with hard rock, glam, and gothic aesthetics. X Japan, BUCK-TICK, Dir en grey, and the GazettE are defining acts; it became a major cultural export in the 2000s via anime and online fandom.
genres.summary: Japanese rock movement fusing elaborate theatricality and costumes with glam-metal and gothic aesthetics — X Japan and Dir en grey as its icons…

genres.name: K-Hip-Hop
genres.description: K-hip-hop (Korean hip-hop) developed from imported American styles in the early 1990s and gradually forged a distinct Korean identity, addressing social issues and cultural identity. Artists like Jay Park, Epik High, and the SMTM franchise elevated it, and the genre now coexists with and influences K-pop.
genres.summary: Korean hip-hop from 1990s underground origins to mainstream coexistence with K-pop, forging a distinct voice through Epik High and the SMTM franchise…

genres.name: K-R&B
genres.description: K-R&B emerged as a distinct strain of Korean pop in the 2010s, influenced by contemporary American R&B, with more introspective, mature themes than mainstream K-pop. Dean, Crush, Heize, and pH-1 built a devoted domestic and international following.
genres.summary: Korean R&B subgenre from the 2010s influenced by contemporary American R&B — Dean, Crush, and Heize's more introspective alternative to mainstream K-pop…

genres.name: Tango
genres.description: Tango originated in the working-class ports and suburbs of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century, fusing African rhythms, European polka, and milonga. It became a global dance craze in the 1920s and was declared a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009.
genres.summary: Buenos Aires port genre fusing African rhythms, polka, and milonga into one of the world's great couple dances — UNESCO Intangible Heritage since 2009…

genres.name: Latin Pop
genres.description: Latin pop blends Spanish-language songwriting with mainstream pop production, gaining international prominence through artists like Julio Iglesias in the 1970s–80s and exploding with the Latin pop boom of the late 1990s (Ricky Martin, Jennifer Lopez, Shakira) and 2010s streaming era.
genres.summary: Spanish-language pop genre that dominated international charts in the late 1990s boom through Ricky Martin and Shakira and into the streaming era…

genres.name: Latin Jazz
genres.description: Latin jazz fuses Afro-Cuban and Brazilian rhythmic structures — clave, bossa nova, samba — with jazz harmony and improvisation. Tito Puente, Chucho Valdés, and later Arturo Sandoval and Paquito D'Rivera built a genre that spans Afro-Cuban jazz to Bossa Nova and beyond.
genres.summary: Fusion of Afro-Cuban and Brazilian rhythms with jazz improvisation and harmony — Tito Puente and Chucho Valdés as its foundational figures…

genres.name: Latin Rock
genres.description: Latin rock emerged in 1960s California, blending rock guitar with Afro-Cuban percussion and Latin rhythms. Carlos Santana defined its sound in 1969, and subsequent generations — Los Lobos, Maná, Molotov, and Café Tacvba — broadened it into a pan-American genre.
genres.summary: Genre blending rock guitar with Afro-Cuban percussion, defined by Carlos Santana in 1969 and developed by pan-American acts like Maná and Café Tacvba…

genres.name: Chanson Française
genres.description: Chanson française is France's lyric-centred popular song tradition, prioritising poetic text and emotional expression over rhythm. Édith Piaf, Charles Aznavour, Jacques Brel, and later Françoise Hardy and Serge Gainsbourg defined its artistry; it remains central to French cultural identity.
genres.summary: French lyric-centred popular song tradition prioritising poetic text — Piaf, Aznavour, and Gainsbourg's genre, central to French cultural identity…

genres.name: French Rap
genres.description: French rap emerged in the late 1980s in Paris suburbs populated by North and sub-Saharan African and Caribbean communities, giving voice to immigration, racism, and precarity. IAM, NTM, and MC Solaar established it; Booba, Jul, and Nekfeu made it France's dominant pop genre.
genres.summary: French hip-hop rooted in Parisian suburb communities, from IAM and NTM's political 1990s to Booba and Jul's mainstream dominance today…

genres.name: Afropop
genres.description: Afropop (or Afro-pop) is a broad umbrella for African popular music from the 1970s onwards that fuses traditional African elements with Western pop and rock structures — distinct from Afrobeats, which is the 21st-century Nigerian-led style. It encompasses diverse traditions from highlife pop to pan-African crossover.
genres.summary: Broad umbrella for 1970s-onwards African popular music fusing traditional elements with Western pop — distinct from and older than the specific 21st-century Afrobeats sound…

genres.name: Folk Rock
genres.description: Folk rock emerged in the mid-1960s when Bob Dylan went electric and The Byrds applied jangling guitars and close harmonies to folk songs. It spawned American country rock, the British folk rock of Fairport Convention and Pentangle, and remains a vital sub-tradition through Fleet Foxes and Mumford & Sons.
genres.summary: Mid-1960s fusion of folk songwriting with rock instrumentation — Dylan going electric and The Byrds' jangle, spawning a transatlantic tradition still active today…

genres.name: Celtic Punk
genres.description: Celtic punk fuses punk rock's energy with Celtic folk instruments and melodies — tin whistles, uilleann pipes, fiddles, and accordions alongside electric guitars and drums. The Pogues pioneered the combination in 1980s London; Flogging Molly and Dropkick Murphys built it into a global genre.
genres.summary: Genre fusing punk rock with Celtic folk instruments and melodies — The Pogues in 1980s London, Flogging Molly and Dropkick Murphys globally…

genres.name: Shanto
genres.description: Shanto is an early form of Guyanese popular song developed in the 1920s by the entertainer Bill Rogers (Augustus Hinds), who set witty, topical commentary to a light guitar accompaniment and an Afro-Caribbean lilt. Its lyrics are steeply local, cataloguing Guyanese places, foods and customs, and his recordings from the 1930s are among the earliest documents of the country's popular music. Shanto sits close to calypso but is distinguished by its storytelling detail and its rootedness in coastal Guyanese life.
genres.summary: Early Guyanese topical song genre pioneered by Bill Rogers in the 1920s.

genres.name: Chutney Soca
genres.description: Chutney soca is an Indo-Caribbean dance-music hybrid that fuses the Bhojpuri-derived melodies and hand-percussion of chutney with the driving rhythm and brass of soca. It crystallised in the late 1980s across Trinidad and Guyana, where descendants of nineteenth-century Indian indentured labourers blended dholak, harmonium and tabla with Caribbean party music. Sung in a mix of English, Hindi and Bhojpuri, it became a carnival and fete staple celebrated through competitions such as the Chutney Soca Monarch.
genres.summary: Indo-Caribbean fusion of chutney and soca, popular in Guyana and Trinidad.

genres.name: Kawina
genres.description: Kawina is an Afro-Surinamese Creole music and dance that took shape in the decades after the 1863 abolition of slavery, drawing on the older banya, laku and tuka traditions. Built on interlocking percussion, including the large skratji drum, and call-and-response singing, its songs treat everyday life, romance and social scandal over long, improvised percussion breaks. Kawina is closely tied to the Afro-Surinamese Winti religion, from which much of its rhythmic vocabulary descends.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Kawina is historically intertwined with Winti, the Afro-Surinamese ancestral religion, and some of its rhythms and songs carry spiritual and ceremonial significance beyond their recreational use. This entry documents the genre respectfully from public scholarly and journalistic sources and is not intended to reproduce sacred or restricted ritual material.
genres.summary: Afro-Surinamese Creole percussion-and-song tradition tied to the Winti religion.

genres.name: Aleke
genres.description: Aleke is a secular Maroon dance-music genre from the Maroni River region straddling Suriname and French Guiana, performed by Aluku (Boni), Ndyuka and Paramaka communities. It grew out of the social ferment of the gold-rush era, when Creole labourers and Maroon musicians exchanged rhythms, and it is driven by interlocking hand-drums, shakers and handclaps supporting energetic call-and-response vocals. Fast, improvisatory and constantly renewed, aleke serves as both communal celebration and a vehicle for storytelling and news.
genres.summary: Secular Maroon dance-music of the Suriname-French Guiana border region.

genres.name: Kaskawi
genres.description: Kaskawi is a modern Surinamese studio genre that fuses the roots percussion and vocals of kawina with the horn-driven, urban sound of kaseko, adding touches of pop and R&B. Emerging in the late twentieth century, it keeps traditional kawina drumming at its core while layering electric instrumentation and contemporary production. The result is a dancefloor-oriented style that bridges Suriname's folk heritage and its popular music.
genres.summary: Modern Surinamese fusion of kawina and kaseko with pop and R&B.

genres.name: Grajé
genres.description: Grajé is a traditional Creole rhythm and couple-dance of French Guiana, one of the core styles of the territory's coastal Creole culture. It is comparatively slow and graceful, highly codified in its danced form, and its songs often carry a nostalgic, reflective tone. Grajé belongs to the same family of drum-led Guianese Creole traditions as kaseko and kanmougwé.
genres.summary: Slow, graceful traditional Creole couple-dance rhythm of French Guiana.

genres.name: Kanmougwé
genres.description: Kanmougwé is one of the most energetic traditional Creole rhythms of French Guiana, played on the yongwé drum and historically tied to collective labour, its movements evoking physical work. It is a drum-and-dance form central to Guianese Creole heritage, performed at gatherings and folkloric celebrations. Kanmougwé stands alongside grajé and kaseko among the principal rhythms of the region.
genres.summary: Energetic labour-rooted Creole drum-and-dance rhythm of French Guiana.

genres.name: Guarania
genres.description: Guarania is a slow, melancholic Paraguayan song genre created in 1925 by the composer Jose Asuncion Flores, who sought a musical form expressing the introspective character of the Paraguayan people. Set in a lilting 6/8 and typically carried by harp, guitar and voice, often in the Guarani language, it contrasts with the brisker polca paraguaya. Recognised in 2024 on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage, guarania remains a cornerstone of national identity.
genres.summary: Slow, melancholic Paraguayan song genre created by Jose Asuncion Flores in 1925.

genres.name: Polca Paraguaya
genres.description: The polca paraguaya is a lively Paraguayan song-and-dance form that emerged in the nineteenth century as the European polka was reshaped by local rhythmic sensibilities. Felt in 6/8, its signature is the sesquialtera, a hemiola interplay between 6/8 and 3/4 that gives it a buoyant, forward-driving swing, typically voiced by Paraguayan harp, guitar and accordion. Together with guarania it forms the core of Paraguay's folkloric repertoire.
genres.summary: Lively nineteenth-century Paraguayan song-and-dance in hemiola-rich 6/8.

genres.name: Galopa
genres.description: The galopa is a fast, dance-oriented variant of the polca paraguaya, usually instrumental and often performed by the banda tipica ensembles that animate Paraguayan festivals and patron-saint celebrations. It heightens the polca's syncopated drive for communal open-air dancing. Galopa is closely bound to the harp-and-brass traditions of rural Paraguay.
genres.summary: Fast, festival-oriented instrumental variant of the polca paraguaya.

genres.name: Caporales
genres.description: Caporales is a Bolivian dance-music style created in 1969 by the Estrada Pacheco brothers, who drew on the figure of the caporal, the mixed-race overseer of enslaved workers found within the Afro-Bolivian saya of the Yungas. Its music is powered by brass bands and a strident, martial rhythm, with dancers' boot-bells accenting the beat. Now a highlight of festivals such as the Oruro Carnival, caporales spread rapidly across the Andes and its diaspora.
genres.summary: Bolivian brass-band fiesta dance created in 1969, derived from Afro-Bolivian saya.

genres.name: Morenada
genres.description: Morenada is one of Bolivia's most emblematic Andean dance-music traditions and a centrepiece of the Oruro Carnival, blending African, Indigenous Aymara and European elements. Its heavy, rolling rhythm is marked by the rattling matraca and a powerful brass band, accompanying masked dancers who evoke the morenos of the colonial era. Its precise origins are debated among scholars and have been the subject of cultural rivalry between Bolivia and Peru.
genres.summary: Emblematic Bolivian Andean brass-band carnival dance with disputed colonial origins.

genres.name: Taquirari
genres.description: Taquirari is a bright, duple-meter mestizo genre from Bolivia's eastern lowlands, especially Santa Cruz and the Beni, with roots traced to Moxo mission and ritual music. After colonisation it moved beyond its ceremonial setting to become popular creole dance music, its syncopated swing shaped by European social dances. Typically carried by guitar, charango and lowland percussion, it is a signature sound of the Bolivian oriente.
genres.summary: Bright duple-meter mestizo dance genre of Bolivia's eastern lowlands.

genres.name: Bailecito
genres.description: Bailecito is a graceful Andean couple-dance genre of western and central Bolivia that took shape around the independence era, descended from the zamacueca alongside the cueca. It plays on the Andean sesquialtera, the interplay of 3/4 and 6/8, and is typically performed with charango, quena or panpipes, guitar and bombo. Counted among Bolivia's core national genres by the late nineteenth century, it also spread south into north-western Argentina.
genres.summary: Graceful Andean Bolivian couple-dance descended from the zamacueca.

genres.name: Sanjuanito
genres.description: Sanjuanito is a festive Andean genre of Ecuador, rooted in the Kichwa communities of the northern highlands around Otavalo and Imbabura, where it accompanied the June-solstice celebrations of Inti Raymi and the feast of San Juan. Recognisable by its pentatonic melodies, shifts between minor and major, and lively 2/4 pulse, it became one of Ecuador's most iconic national styles, played on panpipes, quena, charango and guitar. It endures today across both Indigenous and mestizo festivities.
genres.summary: Iconic festive Andean genre of Ecuador with Kichwa Inti Raymi roots.

genres.name: Bomba del Chota
genres.description: Bomba del Chota is an Afro-Ecuadorian music and dance from the Chota Valley in the highland provinces of Imbabura and Carchi, carried by descendants of enslaved Africans brought to the region during the colonial period. Centred on the hand-played bomba drum alongside guitar and guiro, it fuses African rhythmic sensibilities with Andean and Spanish melodic influence. More than entertainment, it remains a living emblem of Afro-Ecuadorian identity, memory and resilience.
genres.summary: Afro-Ecuadorian drum-driven music and dance of the highland Chota Valley.

genres.name: Albazo
genres.description: Albazo is a traditional Ecuadorian mestizo genre in a hemiola-rich 6/8, its name derived from the dawn (alba) serenades that once opened days of religious festival. Despite a prevailing minor key it carries a spirited, danceable lilt, usually played on guitar and requinto by village bands. Rooted in both Indigenous and Spanish traditions, it remains associated with highland patron-saint celebrations.
genres.summary: Traditional Ecuadorian mestizo 6/8 genre born from dawn festival serenades.

genres.name: Tonada Chilena
genres.description: The tonada chilena is a lyrical, strophic song form from central Chile, descended from Spanish song and shaped by the Latin American troubadour tradition. Unlike the danced cueca it is meant for listening, typically slow and reflective, sung to guitar or harp and historically performed by women singers known as cantoras. Its many guises, from serenades and wedding songs to romances and Christmas villancicos, make it a mainstay of rural Chilean folk life.
genres.summary: Lyrical, listening-oriented central Chilean folk song form.

genres.name: Trote
genres.description: Trote, sometimes called the Chilean huayno, is an Andean dance-music genre of northern Chile rooted in Aymara and Quechua tradition. Built on panpipes, quena and bombo over a steady, trotting pulse, it belongs to the highland repertoire of the Norte Grande alongside the cachimbo and cueca nortina. It anchors carnival and community festivities across the Andean altiplano.
genres.summary: Andean dance-music of northern Chile, akin to the huayno.

genres.name: Cachimbo
genres.description: Cachimbo is a traditional couple-dance and music of the Tarapaca region in northern Chile, part of the Andean-influenced folklore of the Norte Grande. Handkerchief-waving dancers move to a flowing rhythm related to the cueca family, and from the mid-twentieth century a sung version was popularised by ensembles further south. It remains emblematic of the desert-highland communities where it developed.
genres.summary: Traditional handkerchief couple-dance of Chile's northern Tarapaca region.

genres.name: Calipso de El Callao
genres.description: Calipso de El Callao is an Afro-Venezuelan carnival music from the gold-mining town of El Callao in Bolívar state, born when Trinidadian and other West Indian migrants brought calypso to the region in the nineteenth century. Sung in Spanish and Antillean English over a driving Caribbean rhythm, it fuses Trinidadian calypso with Venezuelan folk elements and is inseparable from El Callao's masked carnival and its 'madamas' and devil characters. It was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2016.
genres.summary: Afro-Venezuelan carnival calypso of El Callao, UNESCO-listed in 2016.

genres.name: Quitiplás
genres.description: Quitiplás is an Afro-Venezuelan music, dance and rhythm from coastal Barlovento, named for the tuned bamboo tubes that produce it. Enslaved communities developed these portable bamboo idiophones after skin-headed drums were banned, striking them on the ground in interlocking polyrhythms beneath call-and-response vocals. It remains a vivid emblem of Afro-Venezuelan cultural memory and resistance.
genres.summary: Afro-Venezuelan bamboo-tube percussion music and dance from Barlovento.

genres.name: Golpe Tocuyano
genres.description: Golpe tocuyano, also called golpe larense, is a folk genre from El Tocuyo in Lara state, a distinctive branch of the Venezuelan joropo family. Emerging from the colonial-era blend of Indigenous, African and European traditions, it is voiced by a string battery of cuatro, cinco and medio cinco with maracas and tambora, and sung polyphonically in two or three interweaving voices. It is one of the central musical symbols of Venezuela's centre-west.
genres.summary: Polyphonic string-band joropo genre from El Tocuyo, Lara, Venezuela.

genres.name: Merengue Caraqueño
genres.description: Merengue caraqueño, also known as merengue venezolano or merengue rucaneao, is an urban dance music that flourished in Caracas from the 1920s to the 1940s. Set apart by its distinctive 5/8 metre, it drew on polka, danza and tango and was long considered risqué for its sensual hip movements before winning acceptance in the city's ballrooms. It is a genre entirely distinct from the Dominican merengue in rhythm, instrumentation and history.
genres.summary: Urban Caracas dance music in a distinctive 5/8 metre.

genres.name: Onda Nueva
genres.description: Onda nueva ('new wave') is a Venezuelan genre invented by pianist and composer Aldemaro Romero in 1968, reworking the traditional joropo through the harmonic language of jazz and bossa nova. Romero swapped the harp, cuatro and maracas for the piano-bass-drums trio of jazz, and the style gained international exposure through the World Festival of Onda Nueva held in Caracas from 1971. It stands as one of Venezuela's most sophisticated art-popular fusions.
genres.summary: Aldemaro Romero's 1968 fusion of Venezuelan joropo with jazz and bossa nova.

genres.name: Fulía
genres.description: Fulía is an Afro-Venezuelan devotional song tradition performed chiefly during the Velorio de Cruz de Mayo, the May vigils before an adorned cross in Venezuela's central coastal regions. With roots traced to the Bakongo of Central Africa, it centres on competitive improvised verse, often in strict décima form, carried by tambor criollo, cuatro and maracas. It is at once a religious observance and a display of poetic skill.
genres.sensitiveDescription: The fulía is performed chiefly within the Afro-Venezuelan Velorio de Cruz de Mayo, a religious vigil before an adorned cross. Its devotional context is documented here respectfully from public sources; this entry records the tradition rather than reproducing liturgical or restricted material.
genres.summary: Afro-Venezuelan devotional improvised-verse song of the Velorio de Cruz de Mayo.

genres.name: Baithak Gana
genres.description: Baithak gana is the Indo-Surinamese folk music brought by indentured labourers from the Bhojpuri-speaking regions of northern India in the late nineteenth century. Rooted in a 'baithak' (sitting) social gathering and sung in the Caribbean Hindustani dialect Sarnami, its ensembles pair the melody-carrying harmonium with the dholak drum and the dhantal, a metal rod adapted from farm tools. It is a foundational strand of Indo-Caribbean music, closely kin to chutney.
genres.summary: Indo-Surinamese Bhojpuri-rooted folk music built on harmonium, dholak and dhantal.

genres.name: Queh-Queh
genres.description: Queh-queh (also spelled kweh-kweh) is an Afro-Guyanese pre-wedding tradition of call-and-response song, circle dance and proverbial speech held the night before a couple's marriage. Descended from the wedding celebrations of enslaved Africans in Guyana, it uses music to counsel, tease and honour the bride and groom and their families, with a leader intoning solo lines answered by foot-stamping, hand-clapping participants. It survives among Afro-Guyanese communities at home and in the diaspora.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Queh-queh (kweh-kweh) is an Afro-Guyanese pre-wedding ritual with ancestral and matrimonial significance rather than a stage performance. It is documented here respectfully from public and academic sources and is not intended to stand in for the ceremony itself or any restricted practice.
genres.summary: Afro-Guyanese call-and-response pre-wedding ritual song and dance tradition.

genres.name: Léròl
genres.description: Léròl is a traditional Creole music and couple-dance of French Guiana, a local variant of the quadrille descended from the formal European ballroom dances of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Danced in elegant dress to a string-and-percussion accompaniment, it belongs to the same family of Guianese Creole traditions as grajé and kasékò, blending African, European and Amerindian influences. It endures as part of the territory's coastal Creole heritage.
genres.summary: French Guianese Creole quadrille music and couple-dance.

genres.name: Rasguido Doble
genres.description: Rasguido doble is a song-and-dance genre of the Litoral region, originating in early-twentieth-century Paraguay and popularised across the Argentine and Uruguayan northeast. Its name refers to a double guitar-strumming pattern reminiscent of tango accompaniment, and though often confused with chamamé it is a distinct Litoral style with a lively, buoyant character and lyrics that are amorous, epic or descriptive. Its popular breakthrough came with Correntine composer Mario Millán Medina in the 1940s.
genres.summary: Lively Litoral song-and-dance genre of Paraguay and the Argentine northeast.

genres.name: Plena Uruguaya
genres.description: Plena uruguaya is a festive Uruguayan popular music built on the rope-tuned tamboril drums of the Río de la Plata, drawing on the Puerto Rican plena and the wider world of tropical dance music. Bright and percussion-driven, with lyrics about everyday life and social themes, it is bound up with carnival and murga culture and developed alongside Uruguayan cumbia as a pillar of the country's tropical scene. It carries a strong imprint of Afro-Uruguayan rhythm.
genres.summary: Percussion-driven Uruguayan carnival music rooted in Río de la Plata rhythm.

genres.name: Cumbia Uruguaya
genres.description: Cumbia uruguaya is the Uruguayan branch of cumbia that emerged in the late 1960s, fusing the Colombian rhythm with Río de la Plata sensibilities, Afro-Uruguayan candombe accents and touches of salsa and merengue. A staple of dancehalls and neighbourhood fiestas, it later fed into the grittier 'plancha' street styles of the 2000s. It stands with plena uruguaya at the centre of the country's tropical music.
genres.summary: Uruguayan branch of cumbia blending candombe accents, born in the late 1960s.

genres.name: Pujllay
genres.description: Pujllay is the ritual music and dance of the Yampara people of Tarabuco in Chuquisaca, Bolivia, performed each March to celebrate the renewal of life and the abundance of the rainy season. Its sound is carried by flutes, panpipes and large drums, honouring the exuberant 'Tata Pujllay' and commemorating a victorious 1816 battle of the independence wars. Together with the dry-season Ayarichi it was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2014.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Pujllay is a sacred ritual of the Yampara people tied to agricultural renewal and the Pachamama, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. It is documented here respectfully from public sources and is not intended to reproduce ceremonial or restricted elements of the ritual.
genres.summary: Ritual music and dance of Bolivia's Yampara culture, UNESCO-listed in 2014.

genres.name: Tarqueada
genres.description: Tarqueada is an Andean genre played by consorts of the tarka, an Aymara wooden duct flute, in ensembles that voice a single melody across three registers over drums such as the wankara. Centred on the Lake Titicaca region of Bolivia, it sounds mainly during the January-to-March Carnival and the Anata festival, marking the flowering of the crops and the coming harvest. Its dense, buzzing timbre is one of the signature sounds of the Aymara altiplano.
genres.summary: Aymara tarka-flute consort music of the Bolivian altiplano Carnival season.

genres.name: Danzante
genres.description: The danzante is an Indigenous Andean dance-music of the Ecuadorian highlands, most emblematic of the Corpus Christi festival of Pujilí in Cotopaxi. Its slow, deliberate 6/8 cadence, marked by pingullo flute and bombo drum, matches the measured steps of the masked Danzante, a figure known as the 'Priest of the Rain' who evokes the flight of the Andean condor. It fuses pre-Columbian thanksgiving to the sun with the Catholic Corpus Christi calendar.
genres.sensitiveDescription: The danzante is rooted in Indigenous Andean ceremony later interwoven with the Catholic Corpus Christi, and the dancer holds a sacred, ritual role. It is documented here respectfully from public sources and is not intended to reproduce restricted ceremonial material.
genres.summary: Ceremonial Andean dance-music of Ecuador's Corpus Christi in Pujilí.

genres.name: Capishca
genres.description: Capishca is a lively mestizo dance-music of the Ecuadorian highlands, especially the provinces of Chimborazo and Azuay, whose name comes from the Kichwa verb capina, 'to squeeze'. Built in a hemiola-rich 6/8 (and sometimes 3/4) closely related to the albazo, it frames a flirtatious courtship dance in which couples test their agility through teasing passes and displays. It carries pre-Columbian roots reworked within highland mestizo culture.
genres.summary: Flirtatious mestizo highland courtship dance-music of Ecuador.

genres.name: Amorfino
genres.description: Amorfino is the signature music of Ecuador's coastal Montubio culture, an improvised sung verse performed as a witty counterpoint duel in which singers trade rhymed coplas to show off their wordcraft. Danced in a loose, cheerful couple form with raised shawls, in duple time, it weaves together orality, music and rural theatre. It remains a defining expression of the farming communities of Ecuador's tropical lowlands.
genres.summary: Improvised sung-verse duel of Ecuador's coastal Montubio culture.

genres.name: Cueca Brava
genres.description: Cueca brava, also called cueca chora or urbana, is the urban Chilean cueca that emerged in the working-class bars and fondas of Santiago and Valparaíso in the mid-1950s. It trades the rural, theatrical tone of the traditional cueca for raw lyrics about city and marginal life, a grittier delivery, and instrumentation built on guitar, accordion, piano and tambourine. Roberto Parra and the group Los Chileneros are its defining voices.
genres.summary: Urban working-class Chilean cueca from mid-1950s Santiago and Valparaíso.

genres.name: Sau-Sau
genres.description: Sau-sau is the most emblematic social dance-song of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), a Polynesian tradition of Samoan origin adapted to Rapanui music and lyrics in the 1940s. Its gentle, undulating hip and hand movements evoke a boat rocking on the waves, framing an amorous story danced in colourful feathered costume. A centrepiece of gatherings and of the Tapati Rapa Nui festival, it reflects the island's living Polynesian culture within Chile.
genres.summary: Emblematic Polynesian social dance-song of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), Chile.

genres.name: Zamacueca
genres.description: Zamacueca is a nineteenth-century Afro-Peruvian dance-music of the former Viceroyalty of Peru, blending Spanish, Andean and African elements and rising to popularity as a dance of the independence era. As it spread and each republic claimed it, the zamacueca gave rise to national forms across the continent: the cueca in Chile and Bolivia, the zamba in Argentina, and the marinera in Peru. It stands as a shared ancestor of much South American couple-dance music.
genres.summary: Nineteenth-century Afro-Peruvian dance-music, ancestor of the cueca, zamba and marinera.

genres.name: Pop Jawa
genres.description: Pop jawa is the popular music of Suriname's Javanese community, descended from the kroncong song tradition that indentured migrants from Java brought to the country. From the 1960s its string-based kroncong ensembles electrified into pop groups with guitars, synthesizers and drum kit, absorbing influences from both North American pop and contemporary Indonesian styles, and its first annual festival was held in 1972. It remains a distinctive Javanese-Surinamese branch of the country's plural music culture.
genres.summary: Electrified Javanese-Surinamese pop descended from kroncong, from the 1960s.

genres.name: Bigi Poku
genres.description: Bigi poku ('big drum music') is an Afro-Surinamese brass-band style that emerged in 1930s Paramaribo, when large ensembles married Surinamese folk melodies to New Orleans-influenced horn improvisation. Built on the booming skratji bass drum, snares and brass, it was a key forerunner of kaseko and a staple of street celebrations. It captures the moment Afro-Surinamese folk rhythm met imported jazz and dance-band music.
genres.summary: Afro-Surinamese brass-band style of 1930s Paramaribo, a forerunner of kaseko.

genres.name: Comfa
genres.description: Comfa (also cumfa or komfa) is the drumming, song and dance of an Afro-Guyanese spirit-possession religion, in which insistent rhythms call forth a pantheon of ancestral and ethnic spirits and induce trance in participants. Descended from West African sacred practice reinterpreted under slavery, it centres on figures such as the Water Mother and is bound to ceremonies of healing and communion. It is one of the deepest African-rooted expressive traditions of Guyana.
genres.sensitiveDescription: Comfa is a living Afro-Guyanese spirit-possession religion in which drumming induces trance, not a stage genre. It is documented here respectfully from public and academic sources; this entry records the tradition rather than reproducing its sacred, ceremonial or restricted elements.
genres.summary: Drumming and dance of an Afro-Guyanese spirit-possession religion.

genres.name: Taan
genres.description: Taan, or taan-singing, is the Indo-Caribbean 'local classical' vocal art brought to Guyana and Trinidad by indentured labourers from the Bhojpuri-speaking regions of northern India between 1838 and 1917. A solo male vocalist ornaments long melodic lines over his own harmonium, supported by dholak and dhantal, in a semi-classical style sung at Phagwah, weddings and Hindu rites of passage. It sits at the root of Indo-Caribbean musical identity and is the wellspring from which chutney later grew.
